results.claim: Namma Metro Phase 2: approved 2014 at Rs 26,405 cr with a 2019 target; state cabinet approved Rs 40,425 cr in May 2025; deadline now December 2026.
results.correct_text: Namma Metro Phase 2 (72 km) was approved by the Union Cabinet in January 2014 at Rs 26,405.14 crore (2011-12 prices). On 22 May 2025 the Karnataka cabinet approved a revised cost of Rs 40,425.02 crore for the now 75 km line. The original target was 2020. BMRCL's December 2026 date for the last section has slipped again: as of October 2026, the Pink Line underground stretch is slated to open by March-May 2027.
results.note: Cost: The Week/PTI, 22 May 2025: 'revised project cost ... from Rs 26,405.14 crore to Rs 40,425.02 crore'. DH (May 2025) says the previous estimate was Rs 30,695.12 cr, so this approval added Rs 9,729.90 cr. The 30 Jan 2014 Union Cabinet date comes from Wikipedia; DH reports the Rs 26,405.14 cr figure, but the PIB release could not be opened (403). The state cabinet first approved Phase 2 on 3 Jan 2012 at about Rs 27,000 cr (Business Standard, 4 Jan 2012). TARGET: DH 19 Apr 2025 calls 2020 'Siddaramaiah's original deadline', and DH 9 Nov 2025 calls Dec 2026 'a six-year delay from the original target'. No source opened supports 2019, which appears only in oneindia. DEADLINE: Swarajya 15 Oct 2026 says the Pink Line underground (Dairy Circle-Nagawara) is slated to open by May 2027 and BMRCL aims to finish work by March 2027; DH reports Minister Krishna Byre Gowda saying March 2027. Phases 2A/2B (Blue Line, approved Apr 2021, Rs 14,788 cr) are a separate project. BMRCL had sought Rs 40,614.27 cr; the Centre had not approved the revision as of May 2025.

results.claim: Bengaluru suburban rail: approved Oct 2020 at Rs 15,767 cr, now Rs 16,876 cr; Oct 2025 deadline missed; airport corridor due March 2030.
results.correct_text: The Union Cabinet approved the 148-km Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project on 7 October 2020 at Rs 15,767 crore. When laying the foundation stone on 20 June 2022, the Prime Minister promised completion in 40 months, i.e. by about October 2025; that deadline passed with no corridor built. On 2 January 2026 the state cabinet raised the cost to Rs 16,876 crore. As of January 2026, K-RIDE targets Corridor 2 by December 2028, Corridor 4 by March or June 2029, and Corridors 1 (KSR-Devanahalli/airport) and 3 by March 2030.
results.note: The Oct 2025 deadline is the PM's 40-month pledge of June 2022 (DH 25 Jan 2026: 'Oct 2025 deadline set by PM Narendra Modi'). It was not the deadline at approval: DH of 7 Oct 2020 said the line was likely to be fully operational around 2026. The 2 Jan 2026 date: DH of 3 Jan 2026 says the cabinet 'met on Friday evening' and 'accorded administrative approval for the revised project cost which now stands at Rs 16,876 crore, up from Rs 15,767 crore'. DH ARITHMETIC ERROR: the same article calls the rise 'Rs 1,019 crore', but 16,876 minus 15,767 is Rs 1,109 crore, so do not quote 1,019. DH 7 Oct 2020 put the cost at 'around Rs 19,000 crore' (sources); Rs 15,767 cr is the figure used by the PMO and later reports. The PIB release could not be opened.

results.claim: Upper Krishna Project Stage III: reconcile timeline (17,207 / 51,149 / 65,000 / 51,148.94 / 87,818; 29,566 of ~1.33 lakh acres).
results.correct_text: On 3 January 2012 the Karnataka cabinet gave administrative approval to UKP Stage III at Rs 17,207 crore (2011-12 prices), to be completed over seven years. In late September 2017 the cabinet approved a revised Rs 51,148.94 crore, and the administrative sanction followed on 9 October 2017. In the Legislative Council in September 2021, the water resources minister said the cost had risen to about Rs 65,000 crore. On 16 September 2025 the Chief Minister said the cost had been revised to Rs 87,818 crore, including Rs 40,557 crore for land. He said 29,566 acres had been acquired and 59,354 acres were still pending.
results.note: TIMELINE: (1) Business Standard, 4 Jan 2012: the cabinet under CM Sadananda Gowda gave administrative approval at 'Rs 17,207 crore as per the 2011-12 prices'. (2) Krishi Jagran, first published 28 Sep 2017 (updated 13 Jul 2019): the cabinet chaired by Siddaramaiah approved Rs 51,148.94 cr. The kalyana draft dated this approval to 2019 from the update stamp. That is WRONG: it was 2017, under Congress, not the 2019 coalition. The South First (16 Jan 2023) gives the administrative sanction as 9 Oct 2017 at Rs 51,149 cr; 51,149 is the rounded form of 51,148.94, so the two are the same figure. (3) The Rs 65,000 cr figure is NOT from Jan 2023. It is Minister Govind Karjol's estimate, given in the Legislative Council (The Hindu via inkl, 15 Sep 2021) and repeated in Kalaburagi (3 Oct 2021). It is a ministerial estimate, not a sanction. (4) Hans India, 17 Sep 2025, reporting the special cabinet meeting of Tuesday 16 Sep: 'Originally estimated at Rs 51,148 crore, the project cost has now ballooned to Rs 87,818 crore'. This is the CM's statement; no revised administrative-approval GO was found. LAND: 29,566 acquired plus 59,354 pending is 88,920 acres, which does not reconcile with the 'about 1.33 lakh acres' in the same article (Karjol in 2021 said 1,33,800 acres). Do not write '29,566 of 1.33 lakh acres'; cite the acquired and pending figures as the CM stated them. Other figures in circulation: about Rs 70,000-75,000 cr (DKS/DH 2025) and about Rs 1 lakh cr (DH, Sep 2024).

results.claim: Upper Bhadra: approved 2003 at Rs 2,813 cr; ~Rs 21,450 cr (or Rs 21,473.67 cr) later; Rs 5,300 cr central assistance announced in Union Budget 2023-24 still not released by Aug 2026.
results.correct_text: Upper Bhadra Stage I received administrative approval in August 2003 at Rs 2,813 crore. In 2020 Karnataka approved a re-revised DPR of Rs 21,473.67 crore (2018-19 prices), with completion targeted for March 2026. The Union Budget 2023-24 provisioned Rs 5,300 crore of central assistance. In August 2024 the Centre told the Lok Sabha that the project was not included under any central scheme, so there was 'no question of sanction of funds'. In August 2026 Karnataka's Chief Minister said the money had still not been released.
results.note: PRIMARY: Lok Sabha Starred Q*257, answered 8 Aug 2024 (Jal Shakti). It says the PIB recommended Rs 5,300 cr, the amount was 'provisioned in the Union Budget 2023-24', the project is 'presently not included under any scheme' and needs updated financial details, and the State targets March 2026. Lok Sabha Unstarred Q1795, answered 1 Aug 2024, gives 'Rs. 21,473.67 crore (2018-19 price level)', approval in 2020, and 5,57,022 acres. Lok Sabha Q2238 (Finance, 5 Aug 2024) records PIB appraisal in Oct 2022. The 2003 figure is for STAGE I only: a government brief (search snippet) gives 'Rs. 2813 Crores dated 23.08.2003', and Swarajya (19 Feb 2022) has 'approved in 2003 with an estimated cost of Rs 2,813 crore'. DH (16 Sep 2024) instead says 'Around 2006, the cost estimate was Rs 550 crore', so do not present 2,813 as the whole-project original. The '~Rs 21,450 cr' (Swarajya) is a rounding; use 21,473.67. Non-release as of Aug 2026 rests on the CM's statement at the Southern Zonal Council (PTI/ThePrint, 20 Aug 2026: 'this money has not been allocated'), not on a Union document. The March 2026 completion target has passed; no completion report was found.

results.claim: Hubballi-Ankola rail line: sanctioned 1996 (or inaugurated 1999); revised cost Rs 3,749 cr ('over 10 times'); stalled over wildlife/forest clearance.
results.correct_text: The Hubballi-Ankola line was sanctioned in the mid-1990s; reports give 1995-96 or 1996, and the Railways told the Lok Sabha it was taken up in the 1997-98 budget. Then-PM Vajpayee inaugurated it in 1999. By August 2024 only earthwork and bridges on the 47-km Hubballi-Kiravatti section were complete. The Railways told the Lok Sabha the rest 'could not be executed for want of forestry and Wild life clearance of 569.64 Ha forest land and related litigations'. Newslaundry put the revised cost at Rs 3,749 crore in January 2023. In October 2025 the Union minister said a revised DPR of about Rs 17,000 crore was awaiting Cabinet approval.
results.note: PRIMARY: Lok Sabha Unstarred Q2628, answered 7 Aug 2024 (Railways). It also says a DPR for a double line is now being prepared. SANCTION YEAR: Construction World (24 Jun 2013) says 'the Railway Board sanctioned it in 1996 and work started in 2001'; Business Standard (2012, snippet) says 1995-96; a Lok Sabha answer (snippet; eparlib unreachable) says it was 'taken up in the Budget 1997-98'. Newslaundry (30 Jan 2023) says 'conceived in 1998' and 'inaugurated by ... Vajpayee in 1999'. Use a range. 'OVER 10 TIMES' DROPPED: this is Newslaundry's characterisation with no base figure given. Lok Sabha tables from 2002-05 (search snippets only) list the project at Rs 997.58 cr, which would make Rs 3,749 cr about 3.8 times, so the tenfold claim is unsupported. Rs 3,749 cr is single-sourced (Newslaundry) and no official document was found. Rs 17,000 cr: DH, 3 Oct 2025 (Pralhad Joshi). 'More than Rs 300 crore spent' (CW 2013) is also unverified against an official source.

results.claim: Shivamogga airport: first awarded 2007, relaunched 2020 at Rs 220 cr, opened Feb 2023 at around Rs 450 cr.
results.correct_text: Shivamogga airport was first taken up as a private (BOT) project in 2007-08, and B S Yediyurappa laid its foundation stone in June 2008. The contract was cancelled in 2015 with the airport unbuilt. The state relaunched it on 15 June 2020 at Rs 220 crore and raised the cost to Rs 384 crore in December 2020 to handle A320 aircraft. The Prime Minister inaugurated it on 27 February 2023, and the PMO put its cost at around Rs 450 crore.
results.note: Relaunch: DH, 15 Jun 2020: 'implement it at a cost of Rs 220 crore'; the CM said the work 'had commenced in 2007' and stalled in 2011 over a partners' dispute. Opening: ThePrint, 27 Feb 2023, citing the PMO: 'developed at a cost of around Rs 450 crore'. Rs 384 cr: DH, 19 Dec 2020, which also says the project 'started out with an estimated cost of Rs 40 crore'. DH, 14 Dec 2019, says the cost was revised from Rs 40 cr to Rs 150 cr and that the JV 'bagged the contract in December 2010', which conflicts with a Nov 2007 award (Wikipedia/Organiser). '2007' is safe only as the start of the project, so the publishable text avoids an exact award date. Compare 450 against 220 (the 2020 relaunch) only; the scope was upgraded in Dec 2020.

results.claim: Chamarajanagar HDI rose from 0.576 to 0.601, rank 25th (2005) to 21st (2021/22 HDR).
results.correct_text: According to Deccan Herald's report on the Karnataka Human Development Report 2022, Chamarajanagar's HDI rose from 0.576 to 0.601. Its rank moved from 25th in 2005 to 22nd in 2015 and 21st in 2021.
results.note: DH, 9 Mar 2023, quoted exactly: 'HDI rose from 0.576 to 0.601 and its ranking from 25th in 2005, 22nd in 2015 to 21 in 2021'. DH gives no years for the two HDI values. The state's district HDI dataset compares 2022 with 2015, so 0.576 is probably the 2015 value; do NOT pair 0.576 with the 2005 rank. The figures could not be checked against the primary document: the Economic Survey 2023-24 PDF and the OpenCity HDI CSV both returned 403, and the KHDR 2022 PDF was not found. Treat this as a single press source.

results.claim: MLA/MLC local area development funds: Rs 1,009 cr unused statewide since 2002 (planning minister, 2017).
results.correct_text: On 14 December 2017, Planning Minister M R Seetharam said Rs 406 crore of MLA/MLC local area development funds from 2002-2013 had lapsed unused in deputy commissioners' accounts. Uttara Kannada had the most unspent (Rs 35 crore) and Gadag the least (Rs 3 crore). He said a further Rs 1,000 crore released between 2013 and September 2017 also remained unspent.
results.note: DH (14 Dec 2017) says the 2002-13 lapsed amount is Rs 406 cr, and 'From 2013 till September 2017, a total of Rs 1,000 crore released under the LAD scheme remain unspent'. TNM (15 Dec 2017) reports 'Rs 1,009 crore ... unused since 2002'. That combines two different pots (lapsed 2002-13 funds and unspent 2013-17 releases), and its 1,009 does not match DH's 406 + ~1,000. Avoid 'Rs 1,009 crore unused since 2002'. In DH the Rs 35 cr (Uttara Kannada) and Rs 3 cr (Gadag) figures refer to the Rs 406 cr lapsed pot. No Assembly document was found, so the source is the minister's press statement as reported by two outlets.

results.claim: NFHS district trend - Tumakuru: child stunting 28.6%->40.3%; child anaemia 53.8%->67.6% (NFHS-4 to NFHS-5)
results.correct_text: In Tumakuru, stunting among children under 5 rose from 28.6% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to 40.3% (NFHS-5, 2019-20), and anaemia among children aged 6-59 months rose from 53.8% to 67.6%.
results.note: Opened the official IIPS NFHS-5 district factsheet (Tumkur) via the Wayback Machine (rchiips.org now returns 404). Row 73: '40.3 28.6'; row 81: '67.6 53.8'. The NITI profile agrees (29%->40%, 54%->68%). NFHS-5 fieldwork in Karnataka was 2019-20.

results.claim: Kodagu 2018 flood houses: 845 promised 'in six months' Nov 2018; 660 of 836 families housed by April 2021 per Deccan Herald; Rs 9.85 lakh per house.
results.correct_text: On 29 November 2018 the housing minister said 845 two-bedroom houses for Kodagu's flood victims would be ready in six months, at Rs 9.85 lakh each plus Rs 32 crore for infrastructure. On 23 April 2021, about two and a half years later, the district minister said 786 of the 836 families who lost homes had received houses. Deccan Herald's village-wise count of handovers in the same report adds up to 660.
results.note: DH, 30 Nov 2018 (minister U T Khader, speaking 'on Thursday', 29 Nov): 'ready by six months', '845 two-bedroom houses', 'Each house costs Rs 9.85 lakh'. DH, 23 Apr 2021: Minister V Somanna said 'A total of 836 families had lost homes ... Houses have been handed over to 786 beneficiaries so far'; RGRHCL said Rs 9.85 lakh was 'utilised on each house'. The 660 is the sum of DH's own list (35+80+383+162), not an official count. The list may be internally inconsistent: the same article says the day's 162 houses were 22 in Biligere and 140 in Galibeedu, yet it lists '162 houses in Biligiri'. Saying '660 of 836 housed' on DH's authority alone understates the official figure, so give both. Separately, Infosys Foundation was building 200 more houses. No primary (RGRHCL/DC) document was found.
